Building a file as a descending ladder — each commit closes one layer, its
docstrings naming precisely what is still open — is the right way to work under a
shared ledger. But the commit that closes the **last** layer silently falsifies
every hedge the earlier commits wrote.

opening called a theorem "the one statement this file leaves open" twenty lines

PROVED". A fresh-context audit found them; I had not.

**Why:** these are not sloppy sentences, they are the residue-honesty sentences
the bar asks for. "What this does NOT settle", "what X still owes", "the open
obligation" *read as scrupulous*, so anyone scanning for overclaiming skips them.

costs the next lane a re-derivation of work already at HEAD.

obligation`, `remains`, `not proved` — and re-read each against the code now
below it. Every hit is a candidate false statement, because each was true when
written. Separately grep any **numeral** you corrected in one docstring: a count
fixed in the module header is not fixed 600 lines down in the headline
declaration's own docstring (mine said "four inputs" up top and "one of three"
below). Grep the numeral, not the sentence.
